correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge4\), root dot products give exactly four nonzero squared distances \(2,4,6,8\). At distance \(\sqrt2\), row and column simplices form a good cover with crown-graph nerve. At distance \(2\), source/target closure maps identify the face poset with \(\operatorname{Hom}(K_2,K_n)\), which has an explicit \(S_n\)-equivariant homeomorphism to the \(L^1\)-sphere of the standard real representation; the top character is sign. At distance \(\sqrt6\), missing pairs are exactly the \(N=\binom n2\) opposite roots, so the join is \(S^{N-1}\) with top character \(\det(\bigwedge^2P)=\operatorname{sgn}^{n-1}\). Since \(1<n-2<N-1\), stage homotopy types uniquely fix the integral barcodes. The crown-graph chain sequence proves the degree-one Specht character and finite-group transfer proves the quotient formula. The embedded verifier exhaustively enumerates all faces at two scales for \(n=4,5,6\), exact distances and mod-two boundary ranks, and all \(S_4,S_5\) signed Lefschetz traces. Uniform proof is independent of finite tests.

value.rationale: The \(n(n-1)\) type-\(A\) roots are canonical geometric vertices of the complete-graph symmetric-edge polytope. Their full integral Euclidean Rips persistence across all \(n\ge4\) has structural spheres in degrees \(1\), \(n-2\), and \(\binom n2-1\), including a stage with homology degree far above ambient dimension. The explicit \(S_n\)-equivariant source-target poset equivalence links to graph-homomorphism complexes, while full rational symmetry characters detect a parity-sensitive quotient class unavailable from Betti numbers. This is a natural parameter-uniform topological classification, not an arbitrary finite table or a bare rewriting of the known middle sphere.
